{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
* [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]]
* 1–2 large [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplants]]
* 1 handful plus some more finely chopped [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]], both white and green parts
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] finely-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Green garlic|green garlic]] (optional)
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] fresh [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]]
* [[Cookbook:Cumin|Cumin]] seeds
* Rai ([[Cookbook:Mustard seed|mustard seed]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* 1–2 green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]] broken into 2–3 pieces each
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] (optional)
* ½ teaspoon red [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder (optional)

== Procedure ==

=== Raw method ===
# Wash, then wipe dry eggplant. Apply some oil on the surface of each one of them.
# Blacken eggplants over direct heat. Alternatively, char-roast in an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] or over a fire to infuse smoke.
# Once the skin is blackened and comes away on touch, let them cool a bit and then peel the burnt skin. Reserve the drippings.
# Mash the eggplant flesh by hand until smooth. Transfer flesh to a large bowl.
# Mix in the green onion, green garlic (if using), peas, and salt to taste.
# Heat some oil in a pan. Once heated sufficiently add rai, then cumin seeds, then green chilies. Let the chilies [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for 10–12 seconds.
# Pour this spice mix onto the eggplant mixture in the bowl. Mix well and serve with bhakri and thecha/kharda below.

=== Frying method ===

# Follow steps 1 through 5 as directed above.
# In the step 6 above add turmeric after chilies. Add the eggplant mixture to the pan of tadka. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] for about 1–2 minutes. If required add some of the reserved eggplant drippings to moisten the bharta.
# Serve hot.

=== Kharda/thecha (accompaniment) ===

# Wash and dry about 10–15 green chilies and half handful of fresh coriander. Peel 5–7 cloves of garlic; break the chilies in to 2–3 pieces each.
# Heat about 1–1½ tbsp of oil on the griddle (tava).
# Once heated sufficiently add chilies and garlic (make sure you have exhaust turned on and working).
# Fry them for 30–40 seconds over low heat. Turn the heat off. Now add salt to taste. Put this mix in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] along with chopped coriander and blend it roughly.
# Thecha is ready to serve. While serving put some raw groundnut oil on each serving. This is very very hot dish depending the chilies used. Eat and handle carefully!
